Order No. 07: Dated: 20th January, 2023 Heard the learned counsels for the parties.

It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that this criminal revision application has been preferred against the judgment/order dated 16.02.2022 passed by the A.J.C.-IV cum Special Judge POCSO at Ranchi in Cr. Appeal No. 06 of 2022 by which the appeal preferred by this petitioner has been dismissed and the prayer for bail of the petitioner to enlarge him on bail has been rejected and confirm the order dated 13.12.2021 passed by Principal Magistrate (I/c) Juvenile Justice Board at Ranchi, in connection with Kanke P.S. case No. 182/2021 registered u/s 376 of IPC and u/s 4/6 of POCSO Act, 2012.

sentences.text: It has been pointed out that the charge levelled against the petitioner was that he along with the co-accused persons had ravished a 14 years old mentally retarted girl and when she became pregnant then the FIR was instituted against this petitioner and other accused persons for committing alleged offence u/s 376 of IPC and 4/6 of POCSO Act.
It has been pointed out that the petitioner is innocent.
He has not committed any offence.
He is languishing in jail custody since 20.08.2021.
Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has relied upon the documents as appended with the documents filed in counter affidavit on behalf of the State.

It is D.N.A. test report form the Forensic Science Laboratory, Jharkhand, Ranchi wherein it is categorically found from the present DNA test report that the petitioner is not the biological father of the Ayush Kumar, who is said to be a baby born out of the sexual assault.
Thus the charges levelled against the petitioner is not corroborated Piyush Paul @ Aditya Paul Barla vs The State Of Jharkhand ... ...

1 with the DNA test report.

Further it has also been pointed out that the petitioner is about 15 years old as per the social investigation report, the petitioner is not a criminal by nature and only on the basis of baseless suspicion he has been implicated in this case.

It has also been found from the social investigation report that parents of the child will take care of the petitioner and there is possibility of his coming back in the in the main stream of the society.

It has also come into the case diary that his behavior and nature is very social and cordial and he is very sober and cordial and he is very respectful to the elders and having good behavior with his peers and colleague.

In this view of the matter it has been urged on behalf of the petitioner that there is no possibility of the petitioner to come into the association of any known criminal even if he is enlarged on bail or also not likely to be exposed to any kind mental, physical and psychological danger for this petitioner.
Further, it is also pointed out that the parents of the petitioner are careful and vigilant to the petitioner in future and the petitioner will not involve in any kind of unlawful activities.

On the other hand, learned Addl.P.P. for the State opposed the contentions raised on behalf of the petitioner but did not controvert the fact which come out from the DNA Test that the petitioner is the father of the child has been ruled out.
It is also admitted fact that there is no criminal history against this petitioner and the behavior of the petitioner with his peer group and elders is very cordial and respectful.

Having heard the learned counsels for the parties, this Court finds that if the petitioner is enlarged on bail there is neither any possibility that he will come in association of any known criminal nor any likelihood to be exposed any kind of mental, moral, physical or psychological danger specifically to him and, therefore, for the ends of justice it is found reasonable to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

Accordingly the petitioner is directed to enlarge on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/-
(Rupees Ten Thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned A.J.C.-IV cum Special Judge POCSO at Ranchi in connection with Kanke P.S. case No. 182/2021 registered u/s 376 of IPC and u/s 4/6 of POCSO Act, 2012 subject to the condition (i) one of the bailers shall be parents specifically the father, (ii) mother and father will give separate undertaking that they will take proper care of the petitioner and pursue his further education (iii) any other conditions as the Juvenile Justice Board may deem fit and proper.

The Secretary, DLSA, Ranchi is directed to District Child Protection Officer for conducting counseling of the child intermittently to bring him into main stream of the society and for his overall development.
So that he could not indulge himself in such activities in future.

The Judicial Commissioner, Ranchi -cum- Chairman and the Deputy Commissioner-cum-Vice-Chairman DLSA,
Ranchi is directed to ensure that the directions given to Secretary DLSA is complied with in its letter & spirit.
Let a copy of the order be sent to the Secretary, DLSA, Ranchi to do the needful.
